blocking.section: Decision drivers (Request-path rules); Pros and cons of the options (proxy-wasm as the primary ABI); More information (Revisit bullet)
blocking.issue: The ADR misstates P3 and pack section 8.7 rule 6 in three places. P3 and rule 6 do not forbid remote calls before commit. They require any such call to be declared on the Policy with a timeout and a `failureMode`. Excluding outbound calls is a stricter design choice by the owning document (Excluded rule, OQ-wasm-plugin-system-5), not a rule of P3. As a result, the Revisit bullet claims that admitting outbound calls "would only add Host Functions within v1". That contradicts rule 6 and P3: the change would also need a per-Policy timeout and `failureMode` declaration. The Configuration model defines no such field on `Plugin` or `Policy`, so the Revisit path silently depends on an undefined field. The proxy-wasm con also says timers and shared queues "break pack section 8.7 rule 6", but rule 6 covers only remote calls, and timers and shared queues are not remote calls.
blocking.evidence: L32: "**Request-path rules (P3)**: at most one blocking State Store call per Plugin Policy before commit, none in `onChunk`, no outbound calls." L138: "its outbound calls, timers and shared queues break pack section 8.7 rule 6." L154: "admitting outbound calls would only add Host Functions within v1." Pack section 8.7 rule 6: "Any other remote call before commit, such as a Semantic Cache embedding call to an `AIProvider`, is declared on the Policy with a timeout and `failureMode`." Vision P3: "Other remote calls ... are declared on the Policy with a timeout and `failureMode` (P9)."
blocking.fix: L32: change to "at most one blocking State Store call per Plugin Policy before commit, none in `onChunk`, and no remote call that is not declared on its Policy (pack section 8.7 rule 6); Plugin ABI v1 excludes outbound calls (OQ-wasm-plugin-system-5)". L138: change to "and its outbound calls are remote calls that no Policy declares with a timeout and `failureMode` (pack section 8.7 rule 6), while its timers and shared queues fall outside the per-request model ([Host Function table](../architecture/05-wasm-plugin-system.md#host-function-table), Excluded rule)". L154: change to "admitting outbound calls would add Host Functions within v1, plus a Policy-declared timeout and `failureMode` (pack section 8.7 rule 6) that the Configuration model does not define yet (OQ-wasm-plugin-system-5)".

blocking.section: Decision outcome (rules table, row Results; Figure 2 caption)
blocking.issue: The Results row states the output-buffer rule as universal. The owning document makes body and chunk reads an exception: they take an offset (bodies) and return the bytes written, 0 at the end. `request_body_read` and `response_body_read` take `(offset i64, o, c)`. The ADR's review checklist freezes the "memory convention", so this wording would freeze a convention that contradicts the owning document's Contract and Host Function table. L1-2 raises the feasibility side. This finding covers the contradiction with the owning document, which is blocking under the L2 lens on its own.
blocking.evidence: L53: "an output write above its capacity writes nothing and returns the full length". Owning document, Contract, row Output buffers: "Writes to `(o, c)` return the full length; above `c`, nothing was written and the guest retries. Body and chunk reads return bytes written, 0 at the end". Host Function table: "`request_body_read` | `(offset i64, o, c)`".
blocking.fix: Append this to the Results row: "; body and chunk reads (`request_body_read`, `response_body_read` at an offset, `chunk_read`) instead return the bytes written, 0 at the end". Change the Figure 2 caption to "*Figure 2: the Extism-style buffer convention for one header read inside a Phase; body and chunk reads return bytes written instead.*".

blocking.section: Decision outcome (Figure 1 caption; row Ambient authority)
blocking.issue: The Figure 1 caption says that every guest import passes one Capability gate. The owning document's WASI shim table lists imports whose Capability is "None": `args_*` and `environ_*` succeed with zero entries, `proc_exit` traps with `RZ-PLG-001`, and other `fd_*`, `path_*`, `sock_*` and `poll_oneoff` fail. The owning document states the exception directly: every Host Function requires exactly one Capability, and WASI imports follow the shim table. The ADR's Ambient authority row leaves out the ungated imports. Because the review checklist forbids adding "an ambient import", the ADR needs to name these imports so that the frozen contract matches the owning document.
blocking.evidence: L63: "*Figure 1: every guest import, native or through the proxy-wasm adapter, passes one Capability gate.*" L57: "a `wasi_snapshot_preview1` shim maps log, clock and random calls to their Capabilities and fails file and socket calls". Owning document, Host Function table: "Every Host Function requires exactly one Capability, WASI imports follow the shim table"; WASI shim table: "`args_*`, `environ_*` | None | Success, zero entries" and "`proc_exit` | None | Trap, `RZ-PLG-001`".
blocking.fix: Change the caption to "*Figure 1: every Host Function import, native or through the proxy-wasm adapter, passes one Capability gate; WASI imports follow the shim.*" Append this to the Ambient authority row: "; `args_*` and `environ_*` return zero entries and `proc_exit` traps (`RZ-PLG-001`), all ungated ([Host Function table](../architecture/05-wasm-plugin-system.md#host-function-table))".

non_blocking.suggestion: L77 "ERR_PHASE or ERR_DENIED: RZ-PLG-006" omits `ERR_BUDGET`, which the Capabilities row (L56) and the owning document call sticky. Change it to "ERR_PHASE, ERR_BUDGET or ERR_DENIED: RZ-PLG-006", or add an edge from the State Store node for a second blocking call.

L60 "anything else needs `ruralz.plugin.v2`" states as settled what Release, versioning and compatibility leaves open. Its table has "New optional fields in guest JSON | Pending OQ-release-versioning-and-compatibility-10 | No" and says levels rise while "`rz_abi_version()` still returns 1". Write: "anything else needs `ruralz.plugin.v2`, except optional guest JSON fields (OQ-release-versioning-and-compatibility-10); `rz_abi_version()` stays 1". More information then explains why it cites that Open question.

L24 paraphrases P6 as "a faulty Plugin fails only its own Policy", but P6 says "a faulty Plugin fails its own Filter, not the Node". The meaning matches WG-2 in the owning document. Consider quoting P6's wording or citing WG-2 for the Policy-level phrasing.
